records.issue_text: [BUG] NewResourceServer calls s.Init(ctx) but the constructor's signature is NewResourceServer(opts ResourceServerOptions) with no ctx parameter in scope at this point in the diff hunk, so the reference does not compile unless a ctx happens to be defined earlier in the function body. If no ctx binding exists above line 258, the package fails to build ('undefined: ctx'), breaking CI and every consumer of NewResourceServer; the Init-at-construction behavior is silently unreachable.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] History and Origin no longer call s.Init and dereference s.search without a nil check (unlike Search, which retains `if s.search == nil`), so a server constructed without search configured panics with a nil pointer dereference on the first History/Origin request instead of returning an error. Any deployment of the resource server where the search support is optional (NewResourceServer permits s.search == nil, as Init itself guards with `if s.search != nil`) gets a runtime panic rather than a graceful error on History/Origin calls.
records.rationale: In `pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go`, `History` and `Origin` no longer call `s.Init(ctx)` (removed blocks) and now unconditionally dereference `s.search` (`return s.search.History(ctx, req)` / `return s.search.Origin(ctx, req)`). Unlike `Search`, they do not check `if s.search == nil`. `NewResourceServer`/`Init` explicitly allow `s.search` to be nil (`if s.initErr == nil && s.search != nil { s.initErr = s.search.init(ctx) }`), so a server can be constructed with no search configured, leading to a nil pointer panic on first History/Origin call.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Init() invocations were stripped from all eleven RPC handlers (Create, Update, Delete, Read, List, Watch, Search, History, Origin, IsHealthy, PutBlob, GetBlob) while the Init method itself remains exported, leaving out-of-tree ResourceServer wrappers that relied on the lazy-init-in-handler behavior (or call Init themselves) on silently changed semantics. Any embedding/wrapping code that constructs the server via a path other than NewResourceServer (or that relied on handlers self-initializing) now hits handlers with nil search/watcher state — History and Origin call s.search.History directly and panic with nil-pointer dereference since only the Search handler retains a nil check.

records.issue_text: [BUG] Removing the cacheMu lock from the whole BuildIndex body allows two concurrent builds of the same key to race on the same on-disk bleve directory. Two goroutines calling getOrCreateIndex→build for the same NamespacedResource both pass the cache-miss path and both call bleve.New on the identical file dir (keyed only by namespace/resource/group); the second fails with a file-lock/lock-held error or corrupts the index, and the cache write is last-writer-wins discarding the other build's documents. The old code serialized builds precisely to prevent this.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Removing the build-wide cacheMu lock from BuildIndex and holding it only around the cache write abandons the original serialization contract, allowing concurrent duplicate index builds for the same key. Two concurrent requests for the same NamespacedResource now both run the full document build and both call bleve.New on the same on-disk directory when size > FileThreshold, producing a file-lock conflict error for one caller and wasted duplicate builds in memory for the rest; previously the lock guaranteed a single build per key.
